name: Copper/Gold Ratio: What It Tells Us About Stocks
description: Analyzes the copper/gold ratio as a macro regime signal for S&P 500 forward returns. Copper outperforming gold (ratio rising above 50d SMA) signals economic optimism; gold outperforming copper (ratio falling below 50d SMA) signals risk aversion. Compares 63-day (~3 month) forward SPY returns in each regime. Uses NoAdjustment on both futures to preserve cross-commodity ratio integrity.
source:
# Copper/Gold Ratio → S&P 500 Forward Returns
# Signal: ratio above/below 50d SMA defines rising/falling regime
# Outcome: 63-day forward SPY returns by regime

# --- Data ---
src = market_data_source()()
close = src.c

# Copper futures (HG) — NoAdjustment for cross-commodity ratio
hg_raw = reference_futures(ticker='HG')()
hg = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment
)(hg_raw.o, hg_raw.h, hg_raw.l, hg_raw.c, hg_raw.v, hg_raw.oi, hg_raw.s)

# Gold futures (GC) — NoAdjustment for cross-commodity ratio
gc_raw = reference_futures(ticker='GC')()
gc = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment
)(gc_raw.o, gc_raw.h, gc_raw.l, gc_raw.c, gc_raw.v, gc_raw.oi, gc_raw.s)

# ffill reference data to align with SPY calendar (S42)
copper_close = ffill(hg.c)
gold_close = ffill(gc.c)

# --- Copper/Gold Ratio & Regime ---
ratio = copper_close / gold_close
ratio_sma50 = ma(period=50, type=MAType.sma)(ratio)

# Regime: rising = ratio above 50d SMA, falling = below
is_rising = ratio > ratio_sma50
is_falling = ratio < ratio_sma50

# --- Forward Returns (63 trading days ≈ 3 months) ---
fwd_63d = forward_returns(period=63)(close)

# Split forward returns by regime
rising_fwd = where(is_rising, fwd_63d)
falling_fwd = where(is_falling, fwd_63d)

# --- Win Rate (S29 — dense 0/1 series, NOT where) ---
# Hit rate = % of days where forward return is positive
rising_hit = 1.0 if (is_valid(rising_fwd) and rising_fwd > 0) else 0.0
falling_hit = 1.0 if (is_valid(falling_fwd) and falling_fwd > 0) else 0.0

# --- Regime band for context chart ---
# 1.0 when rising, 0.0 when falling — for shaded band overlay
regime_band = 1.0 if is_rising else 0.0

# --- Timestamp for x-axis ---
ts = index().value

# --- OUTPUT 1: Context — Ratio with 50d SMA + regime shading ---
xy_lines(
    title='Copper/Gold Ratio: Is Economic Optimism Rising or Falling?',
    category='Cu/Au Ratio & SPY Forward Returns',
    y_axis_label='Cu/Au Ratio',
    y_axis_dp=4,
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Cu/Au Ratio', color=Color.Blue),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='50d SMA', color=Color.Slate, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Rising Regime', color=Color.Blue, is_band=True)
    ]),
    order=1
)(x_values=ts, y_values=(ratio, ratio_sma50, regime_band))

# --- OUTPUT 2: Punchline — Median 3-month SPY return by regime ---
xy_bars(
    mode=BarMode.series,
    agg=AggregationType.Median,
    title='Stocks Do Better When Copper Leads Gold',
    category='Cu/Au Ratio & SPY Forward Returns',
    y_axis_label='Median 63d Forward Return',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
    y_axis_dp=1,
    x_axis_label='Regime',
    color_by_value=True,
    data_labels=True,
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='Zero')
    ]),
    series=BarSeriesSchema(series=[
        BarSeriesSpec(name='Rising (Cu > Au)', color=Color.Blue),
        BarSeriesSpec(name='Falling (Au > Cu)', color=Color.Slate)
    ]),
    order=2
)(values=(rising_fwd, falling_fwd))

# --- OUTPUT 3: Reference — Stats table with N, median, hit rate, best, worst ---
summary_table(
    mode=TableMode.standard,
    category='Cu/Au Ratio & SPY Forward Returns',
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='3-Month Forward Return Statistics by Regime',
        row_size=5,
        col_size=2,
        row_headers=['Obs (Days)', 'Median Return', 'Hit Rate (% Positive)', 'Best', 'Worst'],
        col_headers=['Rising', 'Falling'],
        cells=[
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count, type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count, type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=1, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=1, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=2, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=2, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=3, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Max, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=3, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Max, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=4, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Min, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=4, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Min, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1)
        ]
    ),
    order=0
)(rising_fwd, falling_fwd, rising_fwd, falling_fwd, rising_hit, falling_hit, rising_fwd, falling_fwd, rising_fwd, falling_fwd)
